lines.text: Schools are being asked to pay for AI, one student at a time.
And student conversations leave the building.
There is another way.
Umanah AI Lab: a school-owned AI learning lab. One box at school serves the whole class, even with the internet unplugged.
A student signs in from any browser at school.
Ask. Learn. Build. Explore. Progress.
Ask: a tutor that runs on the box. Nothing leaves the school.
Learn: courses, lessons and homework from the teacher.
Lessons have practice questions checked by the software, with the tutor beside them.
Build: write and run Python right in the browser.
When code goes wrong, a helper explains the error and gives hints.
In homework the tutor gives hints, not answers. The software enforces it.
Teachers see the whole class at a glance, and who may need help.
Assignments, with the tutor's help level set by the teacher for each one.
Work is reviewed and graded with a comment, and the student is notified.
Safety: every message is screened. Alerts go to the school's own trusted adults, never to Umanah.
The school runs it, and can see how it is doing, in plain language.
Umanah AI Lab
We are seeking about $100,000 to build and pilot the first classroom boxes.
lines.say: We are seeking about one hundred thousand dollars to build and pilot the first classroom boxes.
